claude.sample_unit: ICU discharge summaries (MIMIC-III notes); 60 notes for blinded human review

links.outcome: Reading level of original ICU discharge summaries (Flesch grade level)
links.effect: Original notes had grade level 9.4 ± 1.2 and Flesch Reading Ease 51.2 ± 6.1; simplification reduced grade level to 7.6–8.0.
links.quote: increasing Flesch Reading Ease from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3 and reducing grade level from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0.

links.outcome: Omission and hallucination rates in LLM-simplified discharge summaries
links.effect: GPT-4o few-shot: medication omission 2.2%, diagnosis omission 0.4%; GPT-4o chain-of-thought had perfect faithfulness and 0% hallucination in human review of 60 notes.
links.quote: In blinded human evaluation, GPT-4o with chain-of-thought prompting achieved perfect faithfulness and 0% hallucination, while GPT-4o few-shot showed the best combined faithfulness, readability, and actionability.

unlisted_practices: Prompt-based (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought) LLM simplification of discharge summaries to improve readability
Section-aware constraints on LLM simplification of discharge summaries

links.effect: Flesch Reading Ease increased from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3; grade level decreased from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0.
links.quote: All six prompting conditions significantly improved readability versus the original notes (all p < 0.0001), increasing Flesch Reading Ease from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3 and reducing grade level from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0.

links.outcome: omission and preservation in AI simplification
links.effect: GPT-4o few-shot: similarity 0.844 ± 0.071, lexical overlap 0.638 ± 0.072, medication omission 2.2%, diagnosis omission 0.4%.
links.quote: GPT-4o few-shot provided the strongest automated overall balance of simplification and preservation (similarity 0.844 ± 0.071, lexical overlap 0.638 ± 0.072, medication omission 2.2%, diagnosis omission 0.4%).

screen.reason: The study empirically tests prompting strategies (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought) and deterministic section-aware pipelines as safeguards to prevent omission and hallucination when simplifying ICU discharge summaries for patients.
